Automatic lines
help: On: every player and team gets the lines that fit its own numbers, picked from the ladders below (docs/25). Off: the fixed thresholds above, the same for everyone.

label: Player line ladder
help: Every line the engine scores for players when automatic lines are on. 2.5 = 3+. Tackles start at 2+: almost every outfield player makes 1 tackle, so it says little.

label: Team line ladder
help: Every line the engine scores for teams when automatic lines are on.

label: Lines kept: likelihood band
help: Lines kept per player or team and stat. The lower end decides how ambitious we are willing to get: raise it to drop long shots, lower it to keep them. Of whatever it leaves, the most likely engine.max_lines_per_stat are kept (docs/39, docs/44).

label: Lines kept per player and stat
help: How many lines each player or team keeps for one stat. The most LIKELY lines inside the band are kept, so a near-certain line is never crowded out by an ambitious one. How far down the ladder we go is engine.line_band's job (docs/44).

label: Likely starter: chance to play for full tiers
help: Before lineups, a player with at least this chance to play can be Solid or Strong. On 2015/16 data, pre-lineup Strong for these players came true 83% of the time, Solid 71% (docs/25). 1.0 = only confirmed lineups.

label: Player lines: "if he plays"
help: On: a player's percentage assumes he plays, and his chance to play shows as a lineup badge instead (docs/27). On 93,000 real forecasts this was calibrated: players rated 80-85% reached the line 84% of the time, where the old number sat 8 points low at the top. Off: the old number that folds the chance to play in.

label: Credit for being on the pitch
help: How much of a full match's expectation a player gets just for appearing, before minutes are counted. At 0, the default, a player's expected count scales straight with minutes: twenty minutes is two ninths of a full match. That is right for how MANY he records and arguably wrong for whether he manages one at all, since a substitute comes on to attack and a starter can have a quiet ninety. At 0.3, twenty minutes is worth about 0.45 of a full match instead of 0.22, so short appearances are credited more. Applied everywhere minutes scale a rate, so the players on the pitch still share the team's expected total exactly. Leave at 0 until it has been judged on real results: it cannot be tested on the simulated league, which allocates player stats strictly in proportion to minutes by construction. docs/58.

label: Hide players unlikely to play
help: Before lineups, a player whose chance to play is below this gets no card. With 'if he plays' on, a rarely used player could otherwise show a high percentage. Confirmed lineups always show.

label: Hide lines that cannot move
help: A line only leads a card if its likelihood would move at least this much (in likelihood, so 0.06 is 6 points) between the league's leakiest and meanest opponent for that stat. It stops cards like "9+ shots, 88%" or "1+ shot, 90%", which read the same whoever the opponent is, so they say nothing about this match. Measured on a full run, the lines this catches are exactly those: 7+ shots at 92% moves 0.4 of a point, 1+ shot at 96% moves 1.2. The line is only demoted, never deleted: it stays under "more lines", in the ladder, in the Finder and available to a combo. A line whose movement is unknown is never hidden, and a card whose every line is insensitive still shows, because an empty feed is no better than a dull one. 0 switches it off. Raising it too far switches it off again in effect: once almost every line is below the threshold that last rule takes over and leads go back to what they were. On the measured run, 0.06 changed 10 leads of 134, 0.08 changed 28, and 0.20 changed only 3 for that reason. docs/56.

label: Hide players unlikely to start
help: Before lineups, a player whose chance to START is below this gets no card. This is not the same as "Hide players unlikely to play": a substitute who always gets twenty minutes plays in nearly every match, so his chance to play is around 0.93 while his chance to start is around 0.41, and the other setting lets him through. His number is then built from a mixture of starting and coming on, and shown beside a strip of his starts. 0 switches it off. Confirmed lineups always show. docs/55.

label: Combo: most lines
help: The most lines one combo can hold. The screens read it so the add button can say "combo is full".

label: Combo: correction before lineups
help: Multiply the lines' chances, then multiply by the entry for the number of players or teams (1, 2, 3, 4 or more). Measured on 237,000 real combinations: before lineups the plain product was 11%, 19% and 25% low for 2, 3 and 4. After lineups no correction is needed (docs/28).

label: Team averages: half-life in games
help: A team's game this many games ago counts half in its averages. Best on 27,000 matches, five leagues, 15 seasons (docs/25). 0 = old behaviour (all games equal).

label: Team averages: judged against the opponent
help: For these stats each game counts relative to what that opponent usually allows (or makes). Helped shots, on target, fouls and cards; not corners (docs/25).

label: Team averages: cap per game (league quantile)
help: A single game's count is capped at this league quantile before averaging. A guard against freak games and feed errors; 0 = off.

label: Player averages: prior strength
help: How many team-stat units of league average each player's share starts from. Higher = one big game moves him less. Tested per stat (docs/25).

label: Insights default order
help: edge = most different from the player's or team's usual (default); likely = highest percentage; kickoff.

label: Headline line: highest likelihood

label: Referees: prior (cards)

label: Referees: cap per match (league quantile)

label: Tier rule
help: earned: tiers come from the whole chance and our track record (docs/31). classic: the old cut-offs.

label: Strong: whole chance at least
help: Strong means it happens about this often. A player line counts as chance x chance to play.

label: Strong: low end at least
help: The low end of the range must also clear this.

label: Where the track record's headline band starts
help: The Track record page leads on how often the lines at or above this likelihood came true. A mean over every band can be right while every band in it is wrong, so the page states the band a reader acts on rather than the average of all of them.

label: Track record: results needed
help: Similar finished lines needed before a tier is trusted. Fewer: Strong drops to Solid.

label: Track record: weight of the stated chance
help: Higher keeps the tier closer to the stated chance until results pile up.

label: Player record anchor
help: Blend a player's own hit rate over his last games into the line (docs/32). Stars who clear a line almost every game are no longer held down by the average spread.

label: Anchor: games needed
help: Games played (of his last 40) before his own record counts.

label: Anchor: weight of the model
help: Higher keeps the model's number closer. The record's weight is games / (games + this).

label: Anchor: most weight his record can take
Highest chance we show
help: Anchored lines never show above this. The calibration map still stops at 97%.

label: Team ratings weight
help: How much the team attack-and-defence ratings count in each team total (shots, corners, tackles, ...). 0 = engine regression only (docs/33).

label: Cards: team ratings weight
help: How much the yellow-card team ratings count in the match cards forecast. 0 = old all-time average (docs/33).

label: Game state: lopsided and tempo
help: Adds two things the model can see before kick-off: how one-sided the fixture looks, and how many goals the two clubs' matches usually carry. A side expected to lead sits deeper; an open game has more of everything. Off until engine_ab.py passes it on your data (docs/37).

label: Fit player spread from results
help: Works out how much a player's count bounces around its average from your own results, instead of the fixed numbers in 'Player dispersion'. Off until engine_ab.py passes it on your data (docs/37).

label: A line for each player and team
help: Gives every player and team its own line for each stat: the count it clears about half the time in its usual game, worked out from its own fitted rate rather than one line for the whole league. Stops 'PSG 9+ shots' and '1+ shot' - lines that are true for nearly everyone and so say nothing. With this on, a likelihood above a half means more than that entity usually manages and below a half means less (docs/52). Off until engine_ab.py passes it on your data.

label: Neighbour lines to keep
help: How many lines either side of each entity's own line to work out as well, so the Finder has a range to answer from. 1 gives three lines in all. Only used when 'A line for each player and team' is on.

label: Strong: gap from usual
help: With 'A line for each player and team' on, a forecast is graded on how far it moves from what that player or team usually does, not on how likely it is - at their own half-way line, likelihood says the same thing about everybody. Strong needs a gap of at least this much AND a likely range that sits wholly on one side of their usual (docs/52).

label: Solid: gap from usual
help: The gap from usual a forecast needs to reach Solid. Half this value is the floor for Watch; below that the fixture looks like any other for them and the line gets no tier, so it never reaches a feed.

label: Opponent by position: prior strength
help: 0 = off. Above 0, each forecast also uses what this opponent lets players in that position do (what a full-back allows a winger). Higher numbers trust the opponent's record less. 20 is the tested starting point. The team total never changes, only how it is split between players (docs/37).

label: Expected goals in team strength
help: 0 = off. Above 0, match chances use a second strength model fitted on expected goals as well as the one fitted on goals. Expected goals are steadier than goals, which are few and swingy. 0.5 counts them equally. Needs expected goals in the feed (docs/37).

label: Shots on target measured against the opponent's on-target conceded
help: Off: an on-target forecast uses how many SHOTS the opponent concedes, times this team's own accuracy, so a defence that blocks shots and one that lets them fly on target look the same. On: on-target becomes a market of its own, measured against what the opponent concedes on target, the way shots, corners and tackles already are. Switch on only after engine_ab.py passes it.

label: How important each market is
help: What each market is worth when choosing the one line a card leads with. A line's score is this weight x its lift over usual x its likelihood, so an important market still has to be saying something. Anything not listed counts as 1.0. Order from docs/39 (docs/46).

label: How relevant each market is to each position
help: What a market is worth for a player in THIS position when choosing the one line a card leads with. Multiplies the market weight, so a forward's tackle line has to be far more unusual than his shot line to take the headline. Anything unlisted counts as 1.0, and club and match lines are unaffected because they carry no position. Set every value to 1 to switch it off.

label: How feed cards are grouped
help: player_market (default) = one card per player or team per market, so a good shots line and a good on-target line both surface; player = one card for everything that player has; line = no grouping, every line its own card (docs/46).

label: How 'different from usual' is measured
help: odds (default) compares the change in log-odds, so 'twice as likely as usual' counts the same whether a line is usually 20% or usually 90%. points compares plain percentage points, which favours markets whose base rate sits mid-table because they have more room to move (docs/48). Only affects ranking; the 'usually X%' a card shows is unchanged.
